title: A Ghost for the Drop
premise: Felix Almeida, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, receives calls on a burner phone from Mara Voss — the handler who trained her and died two years ago. The voice leads her to evidence that the network that made her, Halcyon Division, is selling its ghost operatives' identities to hostile buyers, and that Mara faked her death to expose it. As Felix burns safehouses and cuts through the people she once called family, she discovers the buyer's inside man is her own partner, Dario, whose loyalty to duty was always the lie. In the end Felix chooses love over the only identity she was ever given, torches Halcyon's ledger, and walks away with Mara under new names — ghosts no longer for sale.
about_author: Ansel Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime security consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments by day and fiction by night. They live off-grid on a houseboat with two dogs and an unhealthy knowledge of surveillance tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She runs protection detail for a paranoid arms broker in Lisbon, revealing her polished cover story, her packed go-bag, and her rule: never unpack, never belong. When a burner phone rings in her glovebox — a number that shouldn't exist — she answers out of instinct. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness cracked open by one impossible voice.

chapters.title: Voice of the Dead
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The caller is Mara Voss, her Halcyon handler, dead two years by official record. Mara gives her thirty seconds of proof only Felix could verify, then a dead-drop address. Felix verifies the grave is empty. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into dread; the past isn't past.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Felix retrieves a drive containing Halcyon's asset registry — including her own file, marked TRANSFER: PENDING. She realizes 'transfer' means selling her identity to a foreign buyer. POV shifts briefly to the buyer's fixer, codename Ledger, confirming the auction timeline: eleven days. Emotional beat: the horror of being inventory.

chapters.title: Dario
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Her partner Dario Reyes covers for her missed check-in without asking questions — their easy shorthand shows the found-family bond of their small crew. She almost tells him everything, then finds a Halcyon cipher card sewn into his jacket lining. Emotional beat: warmth undercut by betrayal's first cold draft.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, first time. Flashback-interwoven: how she faked her death, why she built the registry leak, and why Felix — not any other ghost — is the only one she trusts to burn it. Present-day Mara watches Felix's safehouse from a rooftop. Emotional beat: love expressed as operational risk.

chapters.title: The Rotterdam File
chapters.summary: Felix hits a Halcyon front office in Rotterdam using Dario's access codes, stealing auction logistics. She leaves the cipher card behind as a message. A silent alarm trips; she escapes by seconds but is now flagged. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Family Business
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She convenes her crew — ex-Halcyon washouts Nia and Okonkwo — and confesses everything. Nia refuses at first; Okonkwo's own file is in the registry. They become her found family against the family that made them. Emotional beat: chosen loyalty declared aloud.

chapters.title: What Dario Knew
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. He reports Felix's Rotterdam breach to his Halcyon control, revealing he's been a mole for three years to protect his brother, whom Halcyon holds. His duty-love conflict mirrors Felix's arc. He argues to keep her alive until transfer. Emotional beat: a traitor who loves his victim.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Seven days left. The crew raids a data broker in Antwerp and learns the auction venue moves constantly — except for a 90-minute window when the buyer's delegation lands in Malta. Mara contacts Felix directly for the first time since the drop. Emotional beat: hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Rooftop Reunion
chapters.summary: Felix and Mara meet face-to-face in Naples. Two years of grief, training, and unspoken love collide; they argue about whether burning the registry will get every ghost killed instead of freed. They plan anyway. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt under fire.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Sent to buy intel from a Maltese fixer, Nia is recognized by a Halcyon wet team and barely escapes, wounded. The crew learns Halcyon has moved the auction up — four days. Emotional beat: the cost of the mission becomes blood, not theory.

chapters.title: Ledger's Gambit
chapters.summary: Ledger's POV. The buyer's fixer suspects the registry leak and sets a trap: a false auction invite seeded with a tracking beacon. Dario must decide whether to hand it to Felix. Emotional beat: the trap tightening around everyone at once.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Dario delivers the invite, warning her obliquely — his last act of divided loyalty. Felix spots the beacon too late; the crew's Malta staging house is hit. Okonkwo is captured. Emotional beat: guilt, and the realization Dario tried to save her.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV, in captivity. He resists Halcyon's interrogator using techniques he was taught by them, buying time while feeding false coordinates. Meanwhile Felix and Mara intercept the interrogation feed. Emotional beat: endurance as defiance.

chapters.title: Brother's Keeper
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Felix confronts him at gunpoint. He confesses everything — the brother, the years of reporting, the reason he warned her. Felix can't forgive him but needs his access codes for the Malta window. Emotional beat: love against duty, both directions, both broken.

chapters.title: Two Ghosts, One Window
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ninety minutes in Malta. Felix and Mara infiltrate the auction under borrowed identities while Nia runs overwatch and Dario feeds Halcyon false telemetry. They reach the vault where the registry master copy sits beside the buyers' bids. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into precision.

chapters.title: The Auction Floor
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The sale begins; Felix sees her own dossier projected on the bidding screen — her life itemized in lots. She triggers the vault override as Mara extracts Okonkwo. Alarm. Gunfire. Emotional beat: reclaiming selfhood by destroying the price tag.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Climax part one, alternating POVs. Felix uploads the registry to every intelligence service simultaneously — mutual destruction ensuring no buyer dares use it. Halcyon's director orders the site scuttled. Dario turns his gun on his own control team to buy Felix's exit. Emotional beat: sacrifice completing his redemption.

chapters.title: Ash and Water
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Escape across Malta's harbor under fire; Okonkwo wounded again, Nia extracting by boat, the auction site burning behind them. Mara takes a bullet shielding Felix — survivable, but it forces the truth neither has said. Emotional beat: confession amid smoke.

chapters.title: What the Network Owed
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent fallout. News breaks of dismantled Halcyon cells; the director vanishes; Dario trades testimony for his brother's release and disappears east. Felix reads his final message: 'You were the real thing. I was the assignment.' Emotional beat: grief without regret.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Weeks later, a rented house in the Azores. For the first time in fifteen years, Felix unpacks the go-bag — drawer by drawer. Mara plants tomatoes badly. Nia and Okonkwo visit with cheap wine. Emotional beat: stillness earned, identity chosen rather than issued.

chapters.title: A Ghost for the Drop
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Felix's POV. An unknown number calls the landline. Felix lets it ring, looks at Mara, and doesn't answer. The phone stops. Outside, rain on the Atlantic. She pours two coffees instead. Emotional beat: the haunting ends not with silence imposed, but silence chosen.
